title: Vikings make QB change: Carson Wentz to start vs. Bills as Kyler Murray deals with injury - CBS Sports
description: Wentz is now starting at QB for Minnesota after the underperforming Murray suffered a hamstring strain
body:
Wentz is now starting at QB for Minnesota after the underperforming Murray suffered a hamstring strain

        The Minnesota Vikings (6-1) are making a change at starting quarterback. Coach Kevin O'Connell announced Thursday that Kyler Murray has a "hamstring strain" and veteran backup Carson Wentz will start for the Vikings against the Buffalo Bills (6-1) on "Monday Night Football" in Week 9. O'Connell said Murray is considered "week-to-week," but they didn't want to put "him at risk of possibly turning this into a more significant injury." Thus, Wentz will get his second start of the season with Max Brosmer serving as his backup."Obviously, there is a ton of confidence in Carson," O'Connell said Thursday. "He's already helped us. Had a major, major role in two wins this year against two really good teams. He's a steadying presence and a guy we know can go in and play good football."To O'Connell's point, the 33-year-old journeyman performed well in the two games he played filling in for Murray after he suffered a concussion in Week 1 against the Green Bay Packers. Wentz came off the bench in the season opener to throw for 133 yards and three touchdowns on 12-of-19 passing in a 39-22 victory. In Week 2, he started the game at the Chicago Bears, and he completed 11 of his 20 throws for 143 yards in a 9-3 rain-soaked victory at Soldier Field. 
Murray, however, hasn't fit well in O'Connell's scheme this season. Murray's -0.11 expected points added (EPA) per dropback is the fifth worst in the entire NFL, ahead of only Cam Ward (-0.12), Tanner McKee (-0.13), Daniel Jones (-0.19) and Justin Herbert (-0.22). O'Connell's offense thrived with Kirk Cousins and Sam Darnold heaving the ball deep down the field to Jefferson and others over the middle of the field. Murray entered 2026 ranking 40th out of 45 qualified quarterbacks in throws of 10-22 yards (intermediate throws) between the numbers (over the middle of the field) in 2025. That's why his connection with Marvin Harrison Jr. failed in Arizona. Just 10.7% of his throws in 2025 with the Cardinals traveled 10 or more air yards downfield, which ranked third among 42 quarterbacks with at least 150 passes last season. This season playing for O'Connell, 34.4% of Murray's throws are traveling 10 or more air yards, which is the 10th-highest rate in the NFL.   The lack of scheme fit between O'Connell and Murray is why the Vikings offense has just 12 touchdowns in seven games this season, the fewest touchdowns by a team with a 6-1 record or better through seven games since Washington in 1982. The only team that has scored fewer touchdowns than the Vikings in 2026 is the winless Los Angeles Chargers with nine. Both the tanking Miami Dolphins (13 touchdowns) and the Deshaun Watson-led Cleveland Browns (13 touchdowns) have found the end zone more often than O'Connell's unit. 
Wentz has a cushy matchup against the Bills in Week 9, with Buffalo entering the week allowing the third-most passing yards per game (254.7) in the entire NFL in 2026.

title: Ranking NWSL quarterfinalists: Gotham FC shield winners, but are they the most powerful? - CBS Sports

body:
It's the most wonderful time of the year, the NWSL postseason. The 2026 NWSL playoffs begin Friday with the quarterfinal rounds between the league's top eight teams. It's the special place where predictions are futile and what happened in the regular season only matters in opinion. That means it's time for a special playoff edition of the NWSL power rankings. Every week through the regular season we brought power rankings for all 16 clubs, and now just eight teams will kick off the playoffs, so of course we're ranking them ahead of the big games. If you're curious where teams landed before the playoffs, check out our previous rankings.Gotham FC clinched the 2026 NWSL Shield on the final matchday of the regular season, Kansas City Current secured a vital home playoff game, Seattle Reign FC clinched the final playoff spot, and Angel City FC extended their unbeaten streak to 10 games. But where do those teams land on the latest special edition of the power rankings?Let's get to the teams:8. Utah Royals FCThe Utah Royals are the feel-good story of the postseason, making the playoffs for the first time in club history. Head coach Jimmy Coenraets and his squad are effective in a counterpress and had an impressive first half of the season, but have been inconsistent since the summer break and have at times struggled against other playoff contenders. 
Kate Del Fava is the defensive star of the show, and the centerback should be considered a finalist for defender of the year. Kaleigh Riehl, Nuria Rabano, and Paige Cronin aid goalkeeper Mandy McGlynn in net. Though injury concerns in the midfield are coming at a tough time for Utah, with a hamstring injury for Mina Tanaka and Narumi Miura managing a thigh issue.The NWSL playoffs are the place where anything can happen, but the Royals are the only team heading to the postseason on the worst run of form. Just one win in their last five games.7. Seattle Reign FCSeattle just squeaked into the playoffs with a final-day win during Jess Fishlock's farewell home game. With the longtime Seattle Reign player retiring after this season, the group will be motivated for a long playoff run, though the goal-scoring question mark is still haunting the team from last year's postseason appearance.
If defense wins championships, then Seattle Reign have put all their eggs in that basket with goalkeeper Claudia Dickey. Centerback Jordyn Bugg has already emerged as a next-gen talent for club and country, and Sofia Huerta is the league's all-time assists leader, and the outside back is crucial to building up play for Seattle.A lot will depend on Sam Meza dictating things in the midfield, and if Maddie Mercado or Mia Fishel can crank up the attacking looks during the playoffs.6. Portland ThornsThere's no reason to doubt a team that has a healthy, in-form Sophia Wilson, and that's exactly who the Thorns have heading into the playoffs. Portland's roller coaster of a season has included a start without Sam Coffey, who left for Manchester City, followed by a season-ending injury to Olivia Moultrie in August.
But first-year NWSL head coach Robert Vilahamn got the team to the postseason, while managing injury absences to Reilyn Turner, Morgan Weaver, and M.A. Vignola. Despite the group being thinner throughout stretches of the year, they've adapted when necessary, with defensive midfielder Jessie Fleming as the glue on the pitch, the Thorns' iron woman this season.5. Washington SpiritThere's no shortage of motivation for Washington Spirit heading into the playoffs. They have lost two consecutive NWSL Championship finals, and this 2026 main event will be hosted at Audi Field, as a neutral site location was selected earlier this year.Trinity Rodman leads the attack with 12 goals this season. The group has had an inconsistent second half of the season, with injuries to key starters, the return of players from maternity leave, and the inclusion of newly acquired players. The club will hope that enough time has passed that newer players are acclimated, but the playoffs are a different beast. 
A bright spot is Algerian midfielder Melissa Bethi's increased minutes and overall production, and impressive hold-up play by fellow newcomer Clara Lavunga. With Hal Hershfelt out for the season in the midfield, the group will rely on Andi Sullivan to disrupt and Leicy Santos to create, while the backline looks to Esme Morgan and Gabrielle Carle to lock things up.4. Angel City FCAngel City are the pure form team in the playoffs. If you're looking for the leading upset candidate, it's them. They carry a 10-game unbeaten streak, and they turned their season around under interim coach Leif Gunnar Smerud, who took over after Alexander Straus was dismissed in June.The goal scoring is spread out, with leaders Sveindis Jonsdottir (10) and Maiara Niehues (9) setting the tone this season with other players stepping up along the way in Taylor Suarez and Prisca Chilufya. The attack truly cranked up the firepower with the midseason trade for Ally Sentnor, who seems to have finally found a club home with Angel City after stints with Utah Royals and Kansas City.
Equally important is the defensive shape. Outside backs Evelyn Shores and Gisele Thompson have elevated their games this season. Thompson has played higher in the second half of the season, adding five goals and four assists, and Shores has contributed four goals and led the team with eight assists. The return of Savy King on the backline shifted Thompson higher, and the reliable duo of centerbacks Emily Sams and Sarah Gorden in front of shot-stopping goalkeeper Angelina Anderson makes them tough to break down.3. Kansas City CurrentFor all the attention and valid doubts around the hiring of head coach Chris Armas and his lack of experience coaching women's pro soccer, the Kansas City Current are back in the postseason and hosting a home playoff game. The group struggled over the first quarter of the season, losing four games to start, and even if part of the coaching strategy may have been to hang on till Temwa Chawinga could get healthy -- it worked. The return of the two-time Golden Boot-winning Chawinga shifted things in April, as she notched an assist in her first game back and has scored 12 goals this year, and she's not the only goalscorer this season. Haley Hopkins' breakout year is the season's underrated club storyline. Traded to the team in 2025 by North Carolina Courage for $50,000 in intra-league transfer funds, Hopkins is now the co-leader with Chawinga in goals (12) scored this season.
Together, they helped Kansas City become league co-leaders in goals scored by a squad this year (54), and the club now has plenty of key players in form as they head to the playoffs.Midfielder Croix Bethune grew into her role after being traded to the Midwest during preseason, and broke the all-time single-season assist record (11). Michelle Cooper's impact after returning from injury with five goals and five assists is equally notable. The team is better when the trio is healthy and together on the pitch, but the roster depth is also a game changer.It's all a reminder that Kansas City Current may be better than they were during last year's NWSL Shield-winning season because they are now battle-tested and still lethal. 
Angel City and the Kansas City Current square off Saturday at 12 p.m. ET at CPKC Stadium in Kansas City. You can watch that matchup live on CBS and Paramount+.2. Gotham FCInjury concerns for Gotham FC are probably the main reason for putting the recent NWSL Shield winners at No. 2 on the quarterfinalist power rankings. Jaedyn Shaw tapping in as a sub on Decision Day and scoring a goal off the bench is a positive sign, but an ankle injury to midfielder Jaelin Howell will have serious implications for the group moving forward. The East Coast side have won two NWSL Championships in the last three years, won the 2026 Challenge Cup in June, and just hoisted the 2026 NWSL Shield; to not consider them a dynasty in progress is just straight haterdom, and honestly, even putting them second on a power ranking could be just as foolish. 
Even with injury after injury, they are loaded. Guro Reiten might be their best acquisition this year, a player who can dominate the flank as a full back, wing back, or outright forward. Sam Kerr's arrival brings another veteran threat in attack, and Midge Purce and Rose Lavelle are simply built for the playoffs as 2023 and 2025 NWSL Championship MVPs, respectively.Centerback Tierna Davidson is a leading candidate for defender of the year following a year-long absence from an ACL injury, anchors the defense (and what's left of the backline), and lightens the load in net for goalkeeper Ann-Katrin Berger. Howell's ankle, Lavelle and Shaw's minutes management, will all be points of concern, but the beauty in Gotham's DNA is the endless possibility that comes with manager Juan Carlos Amoros and his ability to get the most out of his players in the system. That's part of what makes their NWSL Shield win so impressive, because they're built for the playoffs.
1. San Diego Wave FCSan Diego may have finished second to Gotham FC in the NWSL Shield race, but this was still the best regular season in club history, with a new franchise record for wins and total points. They enter the playoffs as the No. 2 seed, in top form on a seven-match unbeaten run, and fueled by both experience and a youth movement in depth. On the sidelines, Jonas Eidevall has elevated the team in his second year from a lower playoff seed to a top contender, making adjustments whenever injury or form came into question. No matter who is in the lineup, it's control the ball and control the game for San Diego.On the pitch, the group is led by Kenza Dali, this year's underdog MVP, a 35-year-old midfield maven who helped mentor Kimmi Ascanio, Melanie Barcenas, and Gia Corley into the season. Rookie outside back Mimi Van Zanten became a bona fide NWSL starter, crucial in inverted play and attacking sequences, and complements an experienced centerback duo in Kennedy Wesley and Kristen McNabb. Fellow rookie midfielder Lia Godfrey added six goals and six assists over a long season.Trinity Byars' 11-goal sophomore season following an ACL injury was exactly what San Diego banked on when they signed her in 2024 following the elimination of the NWSL Draft. They'll either play spoiler to Gotham, or have the most pressure on them after just missing out on the NWSL Shield.

        World champions collide at WWE Crown Jewel, but there's more than a ceremonial title at stake for Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn. They are set to unearth years of Bloodline baggage in Saturday's main event in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.Reigns and Zayn, Raw and SmackDown's respective world champions, were in a very different place nearly four years ago. In February 2023, Zayn, the underdog fighting in his backyard, nearly dethroned Reigns for the undisputed WWE world heavyweight championship. He fell short of that career-defining moment. Zayn eventually won two world titles and can tie up one more loose end by finally beating Reigns.That's not the only Crown Jewel championship set for this weekend. Women's world champion Liv Morgan and WWE women's champion Chelsea Green clash for the women's crown. Similar to Zayn, Green had never won a world title before this year. She shocked the world by winning the interim WWE women's title in a ladder match before graduating to full-time champion. Morgan is one win away from becoming the only person, man or woman, to win a Crown Jewel title twice.Rounding out the card is a Last Man Standing match between Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton, who were pupil and mentor, respectively, nearly two decades ago in The Legacy faction, and a world title tag team title match.With so much action set for Saturday, the CBS Sports wrestling experts sat down to make their picks for who will emerge victorious at Crown Jewel.
WWE Crown Jewel Championship -- World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns vs. Undisputed WWE Champion Sami Zayn: Run 100 simulations and Zayn beats Reigns once. This is the one. There was genuine fan appetite for Zayn, who'd reached new heights after splitting from The Bloodline, to dethrone Reigns at Elimination Chamber in 2023. Invigorated by his hometown crowd in Montreal, Zayn nearly delivered. But WWE was never pivoting from having Rhodes beat Reigns at WrestleMania two months later. Zayn will avenge that loss this weekend, receiving a hero's welcome in Riyadh, albeit a more muted version of the one he got in Montreal. Reigns' world heavyweight title isn't on the line, so he can afford to lose. It won't come without a lot of interference from The 946, who are actively feuding with The Bloodline and seem on track for a WarGames match with Reigns' family, but Zayn will get it done.  Pick: Sami Zayn wins -- Shakiel Mahjouri (also Brent Brookhouse)WWE Women's Crown Jewel Championship -- Women's World Champion Liv Morgan vs. WWE Women's Champion Chelsea Green: Green's run has been positioned as a "fluke" reign that is more short-term than anything. That would make a Green win here fun, but it also seems unlikely. Morgan has The Judgement Day to help push her over the top while making Green look like a scrappy underdog who just got overwhelmed by "the numbers game." Morgan benefits more from the win from a character standpoint, so she likely gets it done here. Pick: Liv Morgan wins -- Brookhouse (also Mahjouri)Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton (Last Man Standing Match): I had hoped that WWE would move on from Rhodes vs. Orton after Sunday Night's Main Event. The company even teased an undisputed WWE title program between Orton and Zayn before going back to the well. It's unlikely that Rhodes loses to his mentor a second time, especially after attempting to give him more edge with the punt. The Last Man Standing stipulation implies finality, so expect Rhodes to carry winning momentum into a new feud. Pick: Cody Rhodes wins -- Mahjouri (also Brookhouse)
World Tag Team Championship -- The Vision (Bron Breakker & Austin Theory) (c) vs. Penta & Je'Von Evans: Breakker and Theory won the belts on July 6 and have not defended the belts a single time on television or at a premium live event. That's a terrible but true fact that shows how little regard the current WWE climate has for tag team wrestling. While Penta has the Money in the Bank briefcase, it seems we're a little ways away from him cashing in his contract, with Roman Reigns dealing with Sami Zayn as well as 946. It can't hurt to give him a tag title run as a way to keep him busy and continue building momentum. If you're not going to use the tag belts as an actual meaningful championship, you can at least use them as a hood ornament for a wrestler you're pushing as a potential future world champion. Pick: Penta & Je'Von Evans win the titles -- Brookhouse (also Mahjouri)

title: How Jason Eck became an 'overnight success' after 23 years of coaching - CBS Sports
description: Kimberly Eck walked into the hospital to visit her doctor on the morning of Dec. 23, 2010. She was due in January, and she wanted reassu
body:
Kimberly Eck walked into the hospital to visit her doctor on the morning of Dec. 23, 2010. She was due in January, and she wanted reassurance that the baby was on track to arrive in the new year. A Christmas birthday, she figured, was the worst birthday a kid could get.The doctor told her not to worry. She wasn't dilated and there were zero signs of an imminent birth.That night, Jason Eck came home late from work at Ball State. The Cardinals had fired Stan Parrish a month earlier, and new coach Pete Lembo had spent some time evaluating the staff and he made his decision on the offensive line coach. Eck was fired.."I went into labor that night and had him on Christmas Eve," Kimberly said. "Literally, it was like my fastest delivery, two hours. So it had to have been stress."
That baby, Palmer Eck, is now a sophomore quarterback at La Cueva High School in Albuquerque. His father, a burly, larger-than-life former offensive lineman with a personality to match, is now the coach at New Mexico and one of the hottest names on college football's coaching carousel.New Mexico had two winning seasons in the 17 years before Jason Eck arrived two years ago. The Lobos are now 7-1, unbeaten in the Mountain West and ranked in the AP Top 25 for the first time in school history. Eck, 49, is 16-5 in two seasons leading the Lobos and 42-18 overall as a head coach.Eck's turnaround projects at Idaho and New Mexico have looked easy, but they haven't been. He spent 23 years as an assistant coach, worked for 12 different head coaches, was out of work about four times and spent one offseason working at a university golf course.
Now everyone in college football wants a piece of him, and Eck knows it."I think the players and coaches are kind of mirrored right now," Eck told CBS Sports. "It's always been this way for coaches, but now with the transfer portal and NIL, what players are going through is the same thing. It's not as public. It's not as visible. There aren't articles on the internet about it. But this time of year our players are getting contacted by agents, and they're saying, 'Hey, we want to represent you, and I think you can get this much money at this place.' And my message to the players is no different than the message to myself."A strong foundationJason and Kimberly started dating when Jason was a graduate assistant at Wisconsin in 2001. 
                                                                    Courtesy Kimberly Eck
                                                            The first time Kimberly saw Jason Eck, he was working the door of a slow Wisconsin bar.One July night in Madison, a friend who had just been dumped talked Kimberly into going out. They went to the Oakcrest Tavern, a pub known for cheese curds, margaritas and beer-league softball players. For reasons she still can't explain, the bar had a bouncer.
He was a Wisconsin football graduate assistant named Jason Eck."I walked in, and I told my friend, ' Oh, my God, he is so good-looking. I'm going to talk his ear off until he asks me out," she said. "And so I did that."They got married in 2002, as he was leaving for a graduate assistant job at Colorado."And I think he knew I wouldn't move unless we were married," she said. "So that's what we did."
Eck had grown up a child of the coaching business. His father, Jay, coached college basketball and became the head coach at Toledo in 1987. In the 1991 MAC tournament, the seventh-seeded Rockets reached the final and lost to Eastern Michigan by one point. Jay was fired within a week. Jason, an eighth grader, had already picked which high school to attend in Toledo, but that — and his new friends — were off the table."One basket probably determined where I went to high school," Eck said, "because if you win the MAC championship game, they're not going to fire you if you go to the big dance."Paying duesJason Eck and son, Palmer, at Hampton University. 
                                                                    Courtesy Kimberly Eck
                                                            Jason loved coaching, but the profession he picked was relentlessly exhausting. For a decade, the job seemed to do everything it could to talk him out of it and into a normal, 9-to-5 job.
Eck criss-crossed the country, jumping from Colorado to Idaho to Division II Winona State to Ball State, arriving just as Brady Hoke left after a 12-0 regular season. Two losing seasons later, the Ball State staff was fired. After the Christmas Eve news about Baby Palmer, Eck took the offensive line job at FCS Hampton for about $44,000, down from his Ball State salary of $75,000. When he left Hampton after a year, the family had 30 days to vacate university housing. Kimberly packed their belongings with three kids, including one on her hip, as Jason went back to work."Three little kids and a Kia Sorento getting boxes from grocery stores," she said. Western Illinois was supposed to be a safe haven for the Ecks. Mark Hendrickson had four years left on his contract when Eck arrived as a position coach in 2012. The Leathernecks went 3-8 that fall, and they fired Hendrickson anyway. Rather than paying buyouts, the school reassigned the assistants to jobs across campus, and Eck was sent to the golf course to service lawn mowers and golf carts, then to a cubicle at the campus transit center.
"That was my third job in three years," Eck said, "so I started looking at it: my next job is going to be my fourth job in four years, we got three kids, we're not making any money."A decade-plus of being chewed up and spit out over and over again had Eck at his breaking point, so he set himself up to leave the coaching business. In 2013, he turned down jobs at a Mississippi junior college and at Valparaiso, then interviewed with FieldTurf for a sales territory in Kansas and Missouri. Eck felt like he had an "in" as a former coach who could relate with other coaches looking for new football fields. The regional manager, however, wanted a career salesman, Eck said."I mean, if I would have gotten offered that job, I would have taken it," he said.
So, after already passing up two coaching opportunities, he started making phone calls, hoping he could find a rare opening in the spring. Through his connections, he heard North Dakota was hiring Minnesota State-Mankato's offensive line coach. So he emailed Mankato coach Aaron Keen, whom he had never met, about a job that didn't exist yet. Keen called back and said he had no opening."And I was like, well, you might," Eck said.Keen hired him. Minnesota State went 11-1, and Keen quickly promoted Eck to offensive coordinator. About a month later, FieldTurf called back with a different position and a job offer."You know what, I gotta stick with this," Eck said. "There's a reason why I'm doing this, but if that offer had come a year later, I probably would not have been coaching anymore."
The next season, Eck's offense put the Mavericks in the Division II national championship game, and Kimberly came along for the trip."I actually got pregnant while we were on that trip," she said. "That's why we named our son Maverick."The family was growing to six – four kids and a husband and a wife. The family was already in debt, but for the first time in a decade, there was a sense of stability and Jason's career was finally on an upward trajectory..
They left Minnesota State for Montana State in 2015. Then, more of the same. They had to leave another job when the school fired Rob Ash. Was the vicious cycle starting again? It was enough to make any man go mad.Did Kimberly ever tell her husband to stop coaching?"Never, never did."Making the most of an opportunityDan Jackson was the young assistant without a family on John Stiegelmeier's South Dakota State staff in 2016, so of course he had a spare room. He wasn't told it also came with a roommate.Eck had just landed a job as South Dakota State's offensive line coach for head coach John Stiegelmeier, who had averaged nine wins over the previous five seasons and was two decades into a long, successful career. Eck had finally found a landing spot with firm ground and a winning tradition."He was driving into town, and I got a phone call. And he was like, 'Hey, pal, this is Jason Eck. Coach Stig says I'm staying with you,'" Jackson said. "... And so I guess Coach Stig promised Eck a place at my apartment without me even knowing."Eck crashed there for a couple of months. The offensive line coach and defensive backs coach bonded over boxing and horse racing. They have since gone to the Kentucky Derby together with their wives.Jackson had already seen Eck work a room during his job interview with the head coach. Stiegelmeier asked every job candidate to teach the staff as if they were players. Eck studied the roster, gave each staff member the name of a Jackrabbits offensive lineman and ran a position meeting."So he was up there sweating in his suit," Jackson said. "And it is still the best interview that I've sat in on to date."During that first season in Brookings, Stiegelmeier told Eck something no head coach had told him before: "I think you will be a very good head coach someday."Head coach? Eck's primary goal was to coach offensive linemen at the highest level, maybe in the NFL. The Jackrabbits won the Missouri Valley Conference that season and advanced to the national semifinals the next two seasons. Eck was elevated to offensive coordinator in 2019 and won the AFCA's FCS assistant coach of the year award that season, which ended in the second round of the FCS playoffs.The COVID-19 pandemic pushed the 2020 season to the spring of 2021, and Eck suddenly had his Friday nights in the fall free. His second son, Jaxton, was a sophomore linebacker at Brookings High, which played in SDSU's stadium. For the first time ever, he sat next to Kimberly in the stands of his home stadium."She'd look over to me every game and just like say, 'It's so weird to be sitting here in the stadium with you watching a game. I'm so used to me being in the stands here and you being down in the field,'" Eck said.Jaxton was maybe 5-foot-10 and 170 pounds. Eck figured he would play college football on the Division II level. SDSU's defensive coordinator at the time was Jimmy Rogers, now the head coach at Iowa State."He loves speed, and he was always trying to find really, really fast linebackers, which again, thanks to the genetics I gave my son, was not his biggest asset as a player," Eck said. "... I'm not going to have any say in recruiting as an offensive coordinator, but if I became a head coach I would have a say in recruiting."The Jackrabbits lost to Sam Houston State in the national championship game that spring. In 2021, Eck finished runner-up for the Idaho State job, and that fall his offense finished ninth nationally in scoring. Then he emailed Idaho's athletic director, Terry Gawlik, whom he had met at Wisconsin when she was an assistant AD. In December 2021, at 44, he became a head coach.The man in chargeIdaho head coach Jason Eck kisses his wife Kimberly during their days in Moscow, Idaho. 
                                                                    Courtesy Kimberly Eck
                                                            Idaho had jumped to the FBS, struggled and dropped down to the FCS. The Vandals were coming off five straight losing seasons when Eck arrived on campus. He took it to the FCS playoffs three straight years and went 26-13. Jaxton, who wouldn't consider his father's scholarship offer until another FCS school offered him, became a first-team All-Big Sky linebacker.Jackson left Vanderbilt to become Eck's defensive coordinator in 2024. The only house he and his wife, Missy, could find for sale in Moscow was two doors down from the Ecks.Early on, the two left before dawn for a recruiting trip in a blizzard. Jackson offered to drive, knowing his boss could not stay off his phone. Eck refused. A Midwest guy, he told Jackson, had no business driving on winding roads yet."I was like, OK, well, all right, you're driving," Jackson said. "And then he proceeded to go through windy, mountain roads as it snowed, checking his phone throughout the drive. I was like, 'Holy shit!" But I still felt safer than if I was driving because he was right. That was a treacherous deal up there."In Jackson's first game as coordinator, Idaho was within a field goal of Oregon in the fourth quarter before losing 24-14. Jaxton was in the zone, making 14 tackles in the near-miss against the eventual Big Ten champions."I've never been around a football player that maximizes his God-given abilities more than that dude," Jackson said.The Ecks had found success after years of searching. The money finally came, too. For years, the family's summer vacation was its annual tax refund: five days in Minneapolis, a Twins game and an amusement park. Kimberly worked as a nanny and in remote customer service for Amazon so she could be around her children. In his first year at Idaho, Eck received a huge, unexpected tax bill and required a payment plan to pay it off."The whole first year at Idaho was getting out of debt," Eck said. "... A lot of the years we were probably negative month to month. We were not getting evicted or anything, but we were accumulating a little bit more debt every month."Breaking good Eck took the New Mexico job on Dec. 14, 2024, the day after Idaho's season ended in the FCS quarterfinals. Eck kept it quiet. Jaxton didn't know until his father told him that night.Eck had three reasons for taking a job at an FBS program that averaged only four wins over the last 17 years. The first was the basketball crowds he saw on TV at The Pit, New Mexico's famous arena"I think a lot of the schools that have been traditionally basketball schools are people probably just choosing good basketball over bad football," Eck said.The second was conference realignment. Boise State and four other Mountain West schools were leaving for the Pac-12 in 2026, and the new, 10-team Mountain West was ripe for a new program to launch itself to the top."I'm 49 years old," Eck said. "New Mexico's never been in the top half of their conference resource-wise in any year of my life."The third reason was athletic director Fernando Lovo, who won over a nervous Kimberly during the interview process. Eck calls him the best AD he has ever been around.Jason has lived in about a dozen states, but had never been in New Mexico. His only impression of the state was what he heard about in the TV show "Breaking Bad," which features a former high school science teacher who becomes a meth kingpin when he is diagnosed with cancer. Now they gush about the food and the fans in Albuquerque. This week, a fan sent Jason home with homemade jelly. At Tuesday night's radio show, someone handed them hand-knit beanies.New Mexico was picked to finish 11th in the Mountain West in 2025, but the Lobos went 9-4, routed UCLA 35-10 at the Rose Bowl and reached their first bowl game since 2016. Eck was named the conference's coach of the year and Jaxton, who followed him from Idaho, was co-defensive player of the year. UNM rewarded Eck with a five-year, $8.75 million contract.Eck, whose burly, 6-foot-4 figure is a rare makeup for a head coach, has become a national phenom because of his fiery sideline demeanor, viral video skits and personable analogies, including a postgame press conference where he compared player rotations and injury management to playing Madden NFL. He's gone ballistic on a player celebrating with a "turnover belt" while the Lobos were losing. Last month, he appeared in a video as a character named "Jeff," a new employee tasked with selling tickets to the Lobos' football games. Everyone in the skit, mimicking "The Office," knows it's just the coach in disguise. "No, I'm Jeff, but I hear that guy's a heck of a coach," he tells a fan at the ticket window.If you sit down to chat with Eck, you're liable to spend an hour discussing football, family and any other topic Eck might sense a personal connection."He knows families,  parents' names," said center Kaden Robnett, a former Idaho walk-on who followed Eck to New Mexico and is now a starter. "He knows my wife's name. He'll talk to my wife about the games, too."This season started with high expectations mixed with bad news. Quarterback Jack Layne, who also followed Eck from Idaho, needed a second elbow surgery in August and is out for the year. In October, Jaxton broke a bone in his shoulder."I'm going to my son, and he's crying on the sideline heartbroken," Eck said. "You're heartbroken for any player on your team that gets hurt, and he's one of our best players, and he's your son. I felt a little emotional, and he's crying because he feels like he's letting his teammates down because he's on the sideline hurt."The family has seen those tears before. In kindergarten, Jaxton took a soccer ball to the face late in a close game. The pain wasn't what made him emotional.New Mexico linebacker Jaxton Eck holds "The Roaster," the trophy awarded to the winner of the annual New Mexico-New Mexico State rivalry, alongside his brothers and sister, and mother, Kimberly, and father and New Mexico head coach, Jason. "I got a bloody nose, and they made me come out because I was bleeding and was pissed because I missed the end of the game," Jaxton said.The linebacker hopes to return against UNLV on Nov. 14 or against Wyoming on Nov. 20 at the latest. For now, he runs the scout team with play cards, and signals in plays during games."He definitely has overachieved the slow walk-on O-lineman genes that I gave him," his father said.Despite the injuries, UNM has kept winning anyway. Backup quarterback Toa Fa'avae has been thrust into the starting role and is one of four quarterbacks with more interceptions than touchdowns to lead a team with a winning record. The defense ranks No. 1 nationally, allowing only 11.9 points per game, and the Lobos lead the nation in turnover margin (plus-17). A crowd of 34,794, the program's largest for a game against anyone other than New Mexico State since 2005, waited out a lightning delay to watch the Lobos beat North Dakota State 21-16 and reach bowl eligibility. Last Saturday, they won at San Jose State for the first time since 1969.Everything is blooming in the desert. Jaxton could have left New Mexico for bigger pastures in January. After last season, he said, teams were offering him NIL deals between $600,000- $700,000. He stayed anyway to play for his dad and be around his four siblings, including his older brother, Quentin, who works part-time with the equipment crew while he finishes his business degree."Money's not the most important thing to me," he said. "I don't love football to make money."His mother has her own theory."It probably helps too that I'll fly him to see his girlfriend in Idaho anytime he wants," Kimberly said. "Let's throw that in there. That's my own NIL deal.""I get to watch three of my boys on the field together," Kimberly said.Earning respect On Tuesday night, the College Football Playoff selection committee released its first rankings of the season. New Mexico was absent despite being ranked 22nd in the AP poll. Boise State was the only Group of Six school in the CFP's rankings at No. 25. That might be the only list Eck's name isn't on these days.Four major college jobs are open, and Eck's name appeared on several media members' lists as a potential hire. Others are projecting other places Eck makes sense if jobs come open. His alma mater, Wisconsin, still has a head coach, and that job is unlikely to open after a turnaround season under Luke Fickell, even though the Badgers were blanked 30-0 last week at Iowa. Four games against unranked teams remain.Colorado is 3-5, and Deion Sanders is in danger of recording a third losing season in four years. The Buffaloes' athletic director is Eck's old New Mexico boss, Lovo, and Eck was once a graduate assistant in Boulder. Eck's buyout is $4 million through the end of this year, but the Albuquerque Journal reported a clause cuts it in half to $2 million for 12 months because of Lovo's offseason departure for Colorado. That full buyout remains if he follows Lovo to Colorado, per the terms.Eck won't promise he's staying for a third season at New Mexico. He has watched the Nick Saban documentary that features the coach telling reporters covering the Miami Dolphins he wasn't taking the Alabama job, only for him to leave for Tuscaloosa."I never want to do that and lie to people and say something that isn't true," Eck said. "I just know this: I think I have a great job. This community has really rallied behind our team and given us great support, and if I ever leave here, I'm going to be very selective. It's going to have to be an incredible opportunity that I couldn't turn down."Transfer portal. Job opportunities. He told his players those decisions can wait until the season is over."I think everybody who's a part of our program -- head coach, assistant coaches, players -- are going to have to evaluate: where am I at right now? Is it in my best interest to come back here next year? Are there other things that are worth pursuing?" Eck said.His agent is already talking to New Mexico about what it can do to improve the program and Eck's resources, but the coach's demands are not only about him."You don't want to walk into the staff meeting (and an assistant say),'Yeah, you turned down this job, but we're all sitting here and you're living comfortably.' Some of my assistants are probably still living month to month," Eck said. "I have that stuff in mind, too."The Lobos (7-1, 4-0 MW) travel to Nevada (3-5, 2-2) for a Friday night game in the Mountain West on the CBS Sports Network. New Mexico enters Friday with a 5.3% chance of reaching the CFP, according to CBS Sports Forecasting & Projections, the third-best odds among the Group of Six. The CFP assures only one G6 team, the highest-placed team in their rankings, are included in the 12-team postseason."We need to stay focused at the task at hand. It's good. It's a positive thing," Eck said. "If we were 1-7 right now, there'd be no articles linking me to jobs and [the players] wouldn't be playing as well as individuals. You'd have less people contacting you. This is a byproduct of us doing well. People realize they must have some really good players at New Mexico for them to be ranked for the first time in school history. They must have good coaches. But the second we start focusing on that shit, or it takes our mind off of what we're doing, we're going to lose value for ourselves. That's really what I want our program to do: create value for you going forward in your life, whether that's staying here and creating more value for players or coaches, or moving on somewhere else to do that."The future is uncertain, yes, but Jackson, now the head coach at South Dakota State, is sure about one thing."He is not going to change," Jackson said. "... I think when people start changing who they are based on where they coach, then they lose themselves and they fail. He's not going to do that."Until the future arrives, whether it be after a Mountain West title or playoff appearance, the speculation will continue."Yeah, it's pretty annoying, honestly," Jaxton said. "I wish people would just, like, be in the moment. That's what I honestly try and do. When people ask me, I just tell them I honestly have no idea what he's going to do. I think both of us are focused on trying to win a championship this year."Cheese and Coffee The Ecks are creatures of habit, maintainers of schedule, and a bit superstitious, Jason most of all. During the football season, he and Kimberly normally meet for lunch on Thursdays at the same restaurant. If they lose a game, they change it up. Right now, their spot in Albuquerque is Cheese and Coffee."If we're winning, we don't change it up and we order the same thing," Kimberly said. "But this week, our week changed because we play on Friday, so the lunch has to be Wednesday."So on Wednesday, two days before New Mexico plays its first game as a ranked team, Kimberly met her husband at Cheese and Coffee. She usually leaves with a pint of the green chile cheese soup to put in the crock pot and heat up on game days for guests.Things are busy for the Ecks, but for the first time life is actually less stressful. Kimberly can still tell you what the bad years cost. When heavy, monsoonal rain hit Albuquerque this fall, the Ecks' home needed repairs. For most of their marriage, that would have meant more debt."Thank God we can actually afford to fix our roof," Kimberly said.

title: Bronny James faces uncertain NBA future after Lakers assign him to G League - CBS Sports
description: James has totaled just 12 minutes across five appearances in his third NBA season
body:
James has totaled just 12 minutes across five appearances in his third NBA season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 5, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:25 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Los Angeles Lakers assigned Bronny James and rookie Cameron Carr to the G League on Thursday, the team announced. James is no stranger to the Coachella Valley Lakers, having spent time with them across his first two seasons. Still, such an early G League assignment isn't exactly an encouraging start to his third NBA campaign.James, the 22-year-old son of LeBron James, played for the Lakers in the playoffs last season out of desperation due injuries, but when the team has been closer to full strength, he has failed to earn more than spot minutes in his first two NBA seasons. He struggled mightily in the preseason this year, as he shot just 4 of 16 from the field. And while he has always been a defense-first player, his size -- 6-foot-2 and 210 pounds -- has limited his upside on that side of the floor. "I thought he had a really nice September and a good summer with us, but I don't think he's played well in the four preseason games," Lakers coach JJ Redick said in October.
        
            
                How Bronny James became the last survivor of Lakers' 2024 draft class -- and why that's not a good thing
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
What's next for Bronny James' career?Despite those preseason struggles, James survived final cuts as the Lakers ultimately waived former No. 17 overall pick Dalton Knecht to get their roster down to 15 players. The move was relatively surprising considering their draft status. While both Knecht and James have fallen short of the team's hopes for them, Knecht was a former first-round pick who had at least held a consistent rotation role early in his rookie season. He fell off after a failed trade to the Charlotte Hornets, but teams typically like to give their own first-round picks as many opportunities as possible to succeed.
Knecht has since signed a two-way contract with the defending NBA champion New York Knicks. He appeared in his first game on Wednesday, a blowout win over the Chicago Bulls, and he notched 10 points in 16 minutes. By comparison, James has scored four points in 12 minutes spread across five appearances this season.
James was drafted in 2024 and became the first player in NBA history to share the court with his father. Now the elder James is a member of the Philadelphia 76ers, and both teams are doing well after their separation. The 76ers have the NBA's best record at 8-1, and the Lakers aren't far behind at 7-2. But with his father gone and the Lakers thriving in his absence, the younger James is in a somewhat precarious position moving forward. His name carries less weight with the organization than it once did, and a team with championship ambitions isn't going to be willing to wait on the development of a second-round pick forever.
James' contract is guaranteed through the end of this season, but not guaranteed afterward. If he doesn't show progress quickly, he could be a trade candidate at the deadline or simply not retained after the season.

        The price for keeping top-end talent is a headache for college football coaches and front office staffs. In the NIL and revenue-share era, retention is just as important as talent acquisition when decisions are made after the season.Breakout on-field production creates potential offseason leverage for teams looking to keep their best players. There are a few players who could see a sizable windfall given their 2026 impact as NIL contracts are negotiated and new deals are locked in.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jesse Legree, WR | Oregon StateThe midseason All-American announced recently that he was returning to the Beavers in 2027 after his breakout freshman season. With a new contract in place for Legree, Oregon State will not have to worry about the upcoming transfer portal cycle or about teams tampering with its prized possession.Through eight games, Legree leads the FBS in receiving yards (1,110) and touchdowns (14), besting Ohio State Heisman candidate Jeremiah Smith in the categories, and his 20.9 yards per catch average is ninth-best in the country. A former three-star recruit out of Baltimore, Maryland, Legree has been the most impactful first-year player nationally and has been rewarded for it.

title: Ravens vs. Jaguars prediction: Does Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore have any chance in 'TNF' matchup? - CBS Sports
description: How to watch, what to know and a prediction as Jacksonville heads to Baltimore to open Week 9
body:
How to watch, what to know and a prediction as Jacksonville heads to Baltimore to open Week 9
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 5, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:11 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In the Week 9 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Baltimore Ravens play host to the Jacksonville Jaguars.Baltimore is coming off a devastating loss to the Buffalo Bills in which Lamar Jackson returned from his ankle injury and was promptly injured on his first play of the game. The Ravens also lost backup Tyler Huntley during the contest, and they are now decimated on offense as they head into Thursday night's game. Jacksonville came off its bye last week and laid the smack down on the division rival Indianapolis Colts, winning 42-7 to improve to 5-2 on the season and further solidify their hold on the AFC South. Trevor Lawrence and the offense are rolling, and the defense has been largely excellent so far this year.Will the Jaguars take care of business on the road, or will the Ravens pull off a shocking upset? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
Where to watch Ravens vs. Jaguars liveDate: Thursday, Nov. 5 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ETLocation: M&T Bank Stadium (Baltimore)Streaming: Amazon PrimeFollow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Jaguars -9.5, O/U 39.5 via DraftKings SportsbookWhen the Jaguars have the ballThe Jags enter this game having destroyed the Colts last week behind a monster performance from their running game. Bhayshul Tuten ran 16 times for 104 yards and a touchdown, while Chris Rodriguez carried it six times for 41 yards and another score. Rodriguez was limited in practice this week with a hand injury but will play on Thursday night. Tuten's status is up in the air after he didn't practice all week due to an ankle injury sustained against Indianapolis. He played through that injury for the rest of the game, but Jacksonville might choose to rest him here. He's a game-time decision.The Ravens are allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season, with a mere 0.8 of those yards coming before contact, according to Tru Media. Jacksonville could have some issues running the ball, especially if Tuten is out, if the Baltimore front can hold up as it has for most of the season. 
The Ravens did get clocked for 146 yards on the ground this past week by the Bills, but James Cook averaged south of 4.0 yards per carry. A lot of the damage was done by Ray Davis late in the game with six carries for 30 yards. Josh Allen also chipped in 30 of his own. Trevor Lawrence obviously isn't as mobile or as involved in the run game as Allen, but he can move, and if the Ravens get out of their rushing lanes, he can make things happen as a scrambler.Lawrence has played extremely well so far this season, completing 65.7% of his passes at an average of 8.5 yards per attempt, with 17 touchdowns (and a league-high 8.6% touchdown rate) against just four interceptions. Lawrence's top target is clearly Parker Washington, who splits his time fairly evenly between lining up out wide and in the slot. The Ravens are 21st in net yards per attempt allowed this season, and their cornerbacks (Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins) largely haven't played up to expectations. Kyle Hamilton remains excellent against both the run and pass in the slot, so one could expect Washington's route split to lean more heavily toward the outside. Jacksonville may lean toward putting him where he can line up against Humphrey, whose struggles this season have been fairly well documented.
Elsewhere on the perimeter, Jakobi Meyers and, to a lesser extent, Brian Thomas Jr. and Josh Cameron are involved. Meyers and Thomas have only combined for three more targets than Washington has, though, so they are more clearly ancillary pieces in the passing game. The box-score expectations for them should be somewhat muted, but they can pop up at any time for key plays. (Thomas did score last week in his return to the full-time WR3 role, for example.)The Ravens, meanwhile, have been relatively stingy against tight ends in the passing game, allowing only 35 receptions to players at the position, so it's probably not going to be the biggest night for Brenton Strange. Tight ends do have six touchdowns against the Ravens, though, so it might be worth it to at least watch out for Strange in the red zone.When the Ravens have the ballYou can throw out all of the Ravens' offensive stats. Not only is Lamar Jackson out, but so is backup quarterback Tyler Huntley. Jacoby Brissett is reportedly on the way to help, but he won't be active on Thursday night.
Emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano entered the game in relief of Jackson and Huntley last Sunday and will make the start on Thursday night. Fagnano, an undrafted free agent out of UConn, went 10-of-21 for 91 yards and an interception against the Bills. He threw most of his passes to the running backs and did not connect with Zay Flowers even once.Expect the Ravens to lean heavily on Derrick Henry and the run game, but do not expect them to find much success. Henry has been struggling of late to begin with (45 carries for 156 yards and a touchdown over the last three games combined), and the Jaguars have allowed 3.4 yards per carry this season — the single-best mark in all of football.Unless Fagnano and offensive coordinator Declan Doyle pull off some kind of magic act, the Ravens are likely not going to be able to move the ball much on Thursday night.
PredictionThe Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease. Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6

The Nerazzurri lost the Derby della Madonnina against AC Milan on Saturday, while AS Roma continue to surge

        Serie A was back this week around Italy, with Inter, the 2025-2026 Scudetto winners, looking to defend the title in the new season. AC Milan, their cross-city rivals, made some key signings in the summer after replacing the coach and the whole club hierarchy after the disappointing end to the last campaign, and they appointed former Manchester United coach Ruben Amorim to lead the new cycle. We've already had several sackings as Fiorentina replaced Fabio Grosso, who was hired in the summer, after three games in charge and called back Paolo Vanoli to lead the team; and Bologna fired Domenico Tedesco after four matches and replaced him with Raffaele Palladino. Over the international break, Parma decided to part ways with manager Carlos Cuesta and appointed Alberto Gilardino, while Venezia sacked Giovanni Stroppa after six defeats in a row and appointed Davide Nicola. The last coach to be sacked was Udinese's Kosta Runjaic, who was replaced by Paolo Zanetti. Let's take a look at our power rankings 10 games into the season: Don't miss all the Serie A action all season long across Paramount+, CBS Sports Network and CBS Sports Golazo Network. From Italy's biggest teams to America's biggest stars, Serie A has it all, and Paramount+ is the home for every minute of the action until a Scudetto winner is crowned. 1. AS Roma (+1)The Giallorossi are at the top of our power rankings now. Not only because they have been the most consistent team of the first part of the season, despite some key injuries, but also because they have the best attack in the league with 28 goals scored in 10 matches so far. Yes, they have a four-point gap with Lazio right now, but they can get there. 
2. Inter (-1)It's not just about the fact they lost the Derby della Madonnina against AC Milan over the weekend, but how they were defeated. Inter have conceded two goals once again in the opening 10 minutes of the match, forcing them to try to come back once again, but this time it just didn't happen. They can't go on like this. 3. Como (--)I'm sure they are a potential Scudetto winner this season despite playing Champions League soccer. They play, alongside AS Roma, the best football in the country and every week they are showing why they should be considered a candidate for the final win. Keep them in your minds. 4. Lazio (--)What can we say about Lazio? They are at the top of the Serie A standings after an incredible start of the season under Gennaro Gattuso. I just don't see them staying at the top for a long time, considering their second lines are not as good as the starting players. However, they can play once per week and focus on the league. 
5. AC Milan (--)They didn't need to win against Inter to show how talented the roster is. They need more consistency every single week even when they face smaller teams. This is where Ruben Amorim and his players need to improve from now on. 6. Frosinone (+1)Ten games, six wins, two draws and only two defeats against Juventus and Napoli. I mean, who could tell before the start of the season? Frosinone coach Massimiliano Alvini deserves the spotlight. 7. Juventus (+1)A good win against Napoli is not fixing all the issues they had so far but it can definitely help. Juventus are slowly coming back but now they need to win more games in a row. 
8. Napoli (-2)The worst start of the season in eight years. Massimiliano Allegri is not showing why Napoli owner Aurelio De Laurentiis wanted him in the summer to replace Antonio Conte but after collecting only 14 points in 10 games, he doesn't have much time left.9. Bologna (+3)Four wins in the last five Serie A games, including the one against AC Milan away. Raffaele Palladino is quickly adapting to the new team and he deserves it. 10. Fiorentina (+1)Paolo Vanoli's side needed this win against Sassuolo to show why he was called back by the Viola owners. Fiorentina deserved more points than the ones they collected so far and they will get them back. 
11. Cagliari (-1)What's going on here? After a solid start to the season, Cagliari lost four games in a row. Despite that, some players such as Daniel Maldini are still delivering good performances and goals. 12. Atalanta (-3)Is Maurizio Sarri's cycle at Atalanta already over? Things are not looking good at all for the former Lazio and Napoli head coach who now desperately needs some good results to keep his job. 13. Torino (--)They are where we expected them to be. Not at the top, not at the bottom. 14. Genoa (+1)Things are finally getting better for Daniele De Rossi as his team won four of the five games played after the last international break and are now getting closer to the top ten. 
15. Sassuolo (-1)There are some rumors about a possible managerial change at the club with increasing pressure on Alberto Aquilani after Sassuolo lost four of the last five Serie A games. 16. Monza (+1)Yes, they lost again, but Ivan Juric's team is much better than the competitors. Keep an eye on Portuguese striker Gustavo Varela, who has scored nine goals in the opening nine Serie A games. 17. Udinese (-1)Another manager sacked: After only one win, Udinese sacked Kosta Runjaic and appointed Paolo Zanetti to replace him. 
18. Lecce (--)This is a team that will fight until the end to avoid relegation but it won't be easy at all. 19. Parma (+1)The first win under Alberto Gilardino, as Parma won 3-0 away against Atalanta. A solid and much-needed win for the former Genoa coach. 20. Venezia (-1)Maybe we got a little carried away after their first win of the season against Napoli. There's still a lot of work to be done.

        Week 10 of the college football calendar has been highlighted since the schedule was released, with No. 23 Oregon's trip to face No. 12 Ohio State among the headliners. However, when the Buckeyes host the Ducks at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS, it will not be two teams vying for a bye in the College Football Playoff, but instead two programs trying to keep their season from unraveling.The Ducks, at 5-3, have already seen their playoff dreams snuffed out, but a win last week against Northwestern brought their offense to life after a coordinator change. Dylan Raiola had his best game as a starter for Oregon in a win over Northwestern, and now the Ducks have real belief they can go into the Horseshoe and pick up a win that could salvage what's been a disappointing season. Ohio State, meanwhile, comes in with a backup quarterback of their own and is searching for answers after a 30-18 loss on the road to USC last week. Luke Fahey will get his second start and first at home, hoping to find more success and keep Ohio State in the playoff hunt after the first CFP rankings put them at No. 12 -- which would be the first team out of the 12-team playoff. The winner on Saturday will enter the stretch run of the season feeling like they've stabilized after a shock to the system in the form of losing their star quarterbacks for the year. The loser, on the other hand, will realize their goals are no longer within reach and face some hard questions entering the offseason. 
Ohio State vs. Oregon: Need to know  Can Ohio State solve red-zone woes?: The Buckeyes moved the ball fine against USC's defense. It was the best rushing performance from Ohio State this season in Big Ten play in terms of yards per carry (4.74), and while Fahey missed some explosives, he still threw for 260 yards. The problem for Ohio State was finishing drives with six points instead of three. Ohio State made four trips into the red zone against USC and came away with just 13 points. Against Indiana, it also scored 13 points in three trips to the red zone, and the inability to come away with touchdowns nearly cost them there too. If the Buckeyes are going to control this game and keep Oregon from building belief it can win on the road, Fahey has to be sharper in the red zone and the Ohio State rushing attack has to be able to help out. Ducks find life after coordinator change: Oregon's offense had its best performance since the win at USC last Saturday afternoon against Northwestern, one week after firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. Interim coordinator Jay Johnson seemed able to get Raiola into a rhythm and keep him there, something the Ducks have struggled with all season (even with Dante Moore). The frustration after the Illinois game seemed to be an unwillingness to stick with what worked -- in that game, it was the rushing attack -- and against Northwestern, once they found some concepts that worked, they went back to the well until proven otherwise. That seems simple, but it's not always easy as a play-caller to not let your mind wander and get too cute trying to stay ahead of the defense. Johnson seems more comfortable just rolling with what works and being aggressive in any spot, which seems to have a trickle-down effect on Raiola and the offense, also playing with more comfort and aggression. 
That's going to be necessary against an Ohio State defense that is quite good but, as USC proved, can be hit for big plays. Oregon can't be afraid to take swings as a road dog, and last week's performance gives it some confidence it can do that effectively with Raiola. Which defense can steal possessions?: With a young quarterback and a red-zone offense that's struggling, the Buckeyes might need their defense to give them a spark. For as good as the Buckeyes have been defensively this season, they haven't been great at turning teams over. They have just four interceptions on the year (94th nationally) and are 48th in total turnovers forced at 11. Raiola has been prone to turnovers for his entire career dating back to Nebraska and will likely present a couple of opportunities -- either with interceptable balls or strip sacks -- for the Buckeyes to steal a possession or two. Ohio State has to capitalize on those chances if they want to help their sputtering offense. On the other side, the best way to make Ohio State tight in this one would be to pick off the young quarterback and make Ryan Day a bit anxious about letting the young man sling it. Oregon has nine interceptions this season (13th in the country), and if they can bait the freshman into an early mistake, it could alter the Buckeyes' game plan and give the Ducks an even better opportunity on the road.

Ohio State should be able to run the ball well, and at home I would expect Fahey and the offense to operate a bit better in the red zone to put touchdowns on the board when they do move the ball. A Ducks offense trying to push it in the passing game should result in big plays (possibly for both teams), and this is a rare big game where I'm anticipating plenty of points. Pick: OVER 46.5

The Tigers (6-2, 3-2 SEC) have already blown out league foes Florida and Texas A&M at home this season and are 13-3 at Faurot Field against league opposition since 2023.Taking on Texas (6-2, 3-2) represents an uptick in competition, but the Tigers shouldn't be lacking confidence. Florida was No. 8 in the AP poll when it arrived at Mizzou on Oct. 3. It left with a 45-17 loss that legitimized Missouri and showed its full potential.Since then, we've also seen Missouri's floor, which was found in a 31-3 loss at Ole Miss on Oct. 17. But after a bye week and a 34-10 "get right" win over Arkansas in Week 9, the Tigers appear to be back on track. The Longhorns are entering off wins over Ole Miss and Mississippi State, but their vaunted offense is still falling short of expectations.Is this the point when everything will start to click for quarterback Arch Manning? If a Texas team that spent four weeks at No. 1 earlier this season is going to meet expectations, a breakthrough needs to come soon.
Texas vs. Missouri: Need to know  Injuries mount for Texas: Injuries are adding up for the Longhorns, who enter this matchup with star receivers Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman listed as questionable. Wingo is dealing with a quad injury while Coleman is working through a shoulder issue. Both have appeared in all eight games for Texas up to this point while combining to catch 11 of Arch Manning's 15 touchdown passes. Star edge rusher Collin Simmons is also questionable after missing Texas' past two games because of an ankle injury. That's a lot of star power in the "questionable" category for Texas. By contrast, Missouri's injury report is nearly clean.Welcome back, Ahmad: Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy made his 2026 debut last week, carrying the football twice in the Tigers' win over Arkansas. The 2025 All-American has been on the mend from a gunshot wound, and his return adds to a running back room that already features the SEC's leading rusher. Jamal Roberts became the conference's first back to surpass 1,000 yards for the season while rushing for 138 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries in a win over Arkansas. Roberts surpassed 200 yards in wins over Florida and Texas A&M last month. Gaining traction against Texas will be tough. No team has averaged more than four yards per rush attempt against Texas.College Football playoff implications: Texas' chance to reach the College Football Playoff will improve to 67.5% with a win, according to the CBS Sports CFB Forecaster. They will drop to 22.8% with a loss. If the Longhorns lose, they would need to win out against LSU, Arkansas and Texas A&M in order to potentially reach the 12-team field as a three-loss team. Missouri's chances to make the CFP will improve to 16.1% with a win. Those hopes would crater to 1.6% with a loss. The Tigers close with Georgia, Kentucky and Oklahoma.

If Arch Manning can just take care of the football like he did last week, Texas can lean on its defense, win the field position battle and put stress on a Missouri defense that showed real vulnerability in losses to Mississippi State and Ole Miss. The Utes have cruised to an 8-0 record, winning six of their eight games by at least two touchdowns. Last week, they thrashed Cincinnati 49-25 behind 534 yards of offense. BYU has been shaky since stunning Notre Dame in Provo, losing in double-overtime to UCF and only beating lowly Arizona State by one touchdown last week. But with wins over Arizona and the Fighting Irish, the College Football Playoff resume still stacks up with the best. The Holy War has been a streaky rivalry over the years. BYU dominated the LaVell Edwards era, winning 19 of 21 matchups. Then starting in 2002, the rivalry moved heavily towards the Utes, with a 14-3 mark. BYU has now won three straight since 2021, including both matchups as members of the Big 12 by a combined four points. The 2026 game could be an all-time classic.   BYU vs. Utah: Need to know  Diverse offense: Utah brought in offensive coordinator Kevin McGiven from Utah State, and the new hire has completely revamped the unit. The Utes often utilize a two-quarterback system, lining up backup Byrd Ficklin all over the field. Behind the innovation, Utah ranks No. 9 in total offense, good enough for No. 2 in the Big 12. Bear on the loose: BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier has been one of the biggest surprises in the Big 12 this season. The sophomore has thrown for 1,750 yards, rushed for 336 yards and scored 19 touchdowns. In an upset of Notre Dame, Bachmeier passed for, rushed for and caught touchdowns. However, his legs have been bottled up the past two weeks, including only 15 yards on 16 carries against Arizona State. The Cougars need his rushing threat. 
Best on best: Utah lost all five starting offensive linemen to the NFL last season, including two offensive tackles. The unit has risen to the occasion behind breakout left tackle Zereoue Williams. However, left guard Kelvin Obot is out for the season with an injury. Colorado was also able to cause issues with their star-studded defensive line. Can BYU also make the Utes' job difficult?         The second of three games between the service academies will take place on Saturday night (7:30 p.m. ET) on CBS when Army hosts Air Force in West Point. For the Falcons, a win on the road would secure the Commander in Chief's trophy after they beat Navy in a 14-9 battle earlier this year in Colorado Springs. If Air Force can beat Army, it'd give them the Commander in Chief's trophy for the first time since 2022. The Falcons are 6-2 and fresh off a win over UConn to get to bowl-eligible, but face quarterback injury concerns and may start freshman Howard Fisher, who began the year as the third stringer. Army, meanwhile, has no questions at quarterback, where it's the Cale Hellums show as the team's leading passer and rusher. Army's problem in its three losses this season, including last week against Memphis, has been on defense, where they're 83rd in the country in scoring defense and are 80th in rush defense. Service academy games tend to operate on a different plane of existence from other games -- take Air Force's win over Navy, two teams that have played largely in shootouts, but ended up in a 14-9 battle. That's what happens when two option attacks go head to head, and Saturday night's showdown will likely be determined by which team can pop a big play or two against defenses well-versed in how to handle the option. 
Air Force vs. Army: Need to know  Air Force QB uncertainty: As mentioned above, Evan Medders is banged up with a turf toe injury and missed Air Force's win over UConn last week, with Fisher taking over. Medders was already a replacement for Liam Szarka, and since Szarka went down with an injury the Falcons have all but abandoned the passing attack. As an option team, the pass game was already secondary, but Medders and Fisher have a combined 23 pass attempts for 128 yards and two touchdowns. There is almost no threat of the pass with either in the game, and Army's defense will be flying downhill looking to stonewall the run game.The concerns with changing quarterbacks in an option attack are whether they'll make the right reads and whether they'll make ball-handling mistakes that lead to turnovers. In a game where points are at a premium, turnovers can swing a game. However, if Medders is compromised as a runner, that's a different limitation, and it might be better to have the threat of the quarterback run than to have someone ailing with a bit more experience. 
Can Cale Hellums create some big plays?: The quarterback advantage is clearly on Army's side, where Hellums is dynamic as a runner and can pop a pass play over the top when the opportunity presents itself. Clock control, field position and ball security are always the name of the game in service academy games because it's so hard to create explosives against defenses so well-versed against the option. However, a dynamic quarterback can change that in either the run or pass game, and if Hellums can create a couple explosive plays at home, that can swing this game in Army's favor. Whether that's making a man miss in space on the outside running it or hitting one of the few shot plays in the passing game they'll attempt, Hellums has to make the quarterback advantage apparent for the Black Knights. The hidden yards battle: Field position is everything in an option vs. option game, and that puts pressure on the special teams units to take care of business. The punt teams tend to get a workout in these games, and getting punts off cleanly and covering them well to force the offenses to do the heavy lifting on gaining yards is key for both teams. 
Both teams have excellent punters averaging over 47 yards per boot and they've been stingy about allowing returns. Air Force's punt coverage unit struggled a touch early in the year, but they've allowed three total punt returns in their last five games for six yards. Army, meanwhile, has given up 33 total yards on six returns all season. If either of these teams can make the other blink in the punt game, it can be as big as a turnover in a game with few possessions. Where to watch Air Force vs. Army live  Date: Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time: 7:30 p.m. ET  Location: Blaik Field at Michie Stadium -- West Point, New YorkTV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com, CBS Sports App  Streaming on Paramount+ Premium
Air Force vs. Army prediction, picks  On paper, these two teams should score plenty on each other, but we know the trends and statistical profiles don't matter much in service academy games. Air Force has played in two games all season against FBS opponents that finished below 40 points, but one was that 14-9 win over Navy. Army has similarly gone over this total in all but two games, but none of that matters. This game will be decided by who creates the handful of big plays -- in any of the three phases of the game -- and who can lean on the other team to try and break them down by the end of 60 minutes. Pick: Under 44.5SportsLine's proven computer model has simulated every Week 10 college football game 10,000 times. description: Smothers was a splashy transfer portal addition for Texas, but he's battled injury all season

        The Texas running back room just got thinner and less explosive. Hollywood Smothers will miss the remainder of the season with a torn MCL, 247Sports confirms.The No. 3 running back in the 2026 transfer class, Smothers was part of a nice haul for Steve Sarkisian, especially on the offensive side of the ball. Smothers was coming off a 939-yard season at NC State in which he totaled seven touchdowns, and expectations were high for him in Austin.However, Smothers has battled injuries all season. He didn't play at all in the Longhorns' road win over Tennessee due to a lower-body injury. Smothers also missed his team's home win over Ole Miss on Oct. 24. In his last three appearances, Smothers has been part of a rotation with Raleek Brown and was ineffective when he did touch the ball.In last week's win over Mississippi State, Smothers carried the ball just four times for minus-6 yards before getting helped into the medical tent.
Smothers will end his season with just 283 yards and two touchdowns in six games. Brown will now be asked to carry a heavier workload in the rushing game.The loss of Smothers is just the latest in a series of significant injuries Texas has suffered with its College Football Playoff hopes on the line this weekend against Missouri. If the Longhorns want any shot of living up to preseason expectations, Steve Sarkisian needs other players to step up in the absence of some stars.Injuries piling up for TexasIf you want to check out the Texas availability report for Saturday's game against Missouri, I suggest you carve out a few extra minutes, because it's a long list. With Smothers already ruled out -- and star left tackle Trevor Goosby recently lost for the season -- some other big names are designated as questionable.
Colin Simmons, EDGERyan Wingo, WRCam Coleman, WRKade Phillips, DBGraceson Littleton, DBAccording to 247Sports, Simmons and Wingo are the two most likely to suit up, but neither one of them is a guarantee. Simmons is still recovering from a high-ankle sprain, and he might need another week to fully heal. Wingo is trying to fight through a quad injury to play in what amounts to a homecoming for the St. Louis native.There's never a good time for the injury bug to bite, but this is especially poor timing for the Longhorns. Texas is sitting on two losses with key road games against Missouri and LSU coming up in the next two weeks. The Horns' offense has already been inconsistent even with Smothers, Coleman and Wingo in the lineup.Because of that, the defense has been the backbone of this Texas team, but how much longer can that unit hold up with a banged-up Simmons and depleted secondary?
Run game stuck in neutralWhen Sarkisian first took over at Texas, the Longhorns boasted legitimate superstars at running back in Bijan Robinson and Jonathon Brooks. Since Brooks left for the NFL following the 2023 season, Texas has struggled to rediscover that magic on the ground.Tre Wisner led the backfield in 2024 -- and while he did rush for 1,000 yards -- he only averaged 4.7 yards per carry. Last season, Wisner battled injury, and his rushing total (597 yards) and efficiency (4.6 yards per carry) were negatively affected.Last offseason, the Horns made running back a priority in the portal and spent up to land Smothers and Brown. That duo provided hope that Texas would be able to gash opponents on the ground in 2026, but that just hasn't materialized.
Texas is only averaging 135.4 rushing yards per game, which ranks 13th in the SEC. Only Oklahoma, Vanderbilt and Arkansas have been worse in that department, which isn't the kind of company an offensive coach like Sarkisian wants to keep.The Longhorns will have to address the running back position again next offseason, but for now, it will be up to Brown and quarterback Arch Manning to make the most of what's available to them on the ground.
